title: Automation

seo.title: Automation | Mohit Walia
seo.description: Workflows that move data between the tools you already pay for, with a person in the loop where judgment matters.

hero.heading: Automation for the work your team repeats every week.
hero.subtitle: I connect the systems you already use so leads, orders, files, and notifications move without someone copying them by hand.

overview: Automation is a workflow with a trigger, a few steps, and a failure you can see. I build those for operations that are currently a spreadsheet and a memory.
problem: The same information is typed into three tools. When someone is out, the process stops, and nobody can tell which copy is right.
solution: I pick the system of record, then automate the copies and the notifications. Failures are visible. A person still handles the steps that need judgment.

features.title: A named trigger
features.detail: A form, a payment, a new row, or a webhook starts the workflow.

features.title: Visible failures
features.detail: When a step breaks, you can see it and retry it.

features.title: A human where it matters
features.detail: Approval stays with a person when the cost of a mistake is high.

process.title: Discovery
process.detail: We pin down the outcome, the constraints, and what the first release has to do.

process.title: Planning
process.detail: I turn that into a scope, a sequence, and the technical approach.

process.title: Development
process.detail: I build in small slices you can review, on the stack this service uses.

process.title: Testing
process.detail: We check the flows that matter before anything is treated as finished.

process.title: Launch
process.detail: I ship it, watch the first days, and leave you with a clear way to change it.

benefits.title: The process survives vacation
benefits.detail: It is not stored in one person's inbox.

benefits.title: You can change a step
benefits.detail: The workflow is code or a clear diagram, not a mystery.

A way to retry a failed run

The happy path and the failures.

faqs.question: Do you use Zapier or custom code?
faqs.answer: Whichever fits the volume and the failure modes. Simple chains can stay in a tool you already have. Anything that needs history or care becomes code.

faqs.question: Can this include an AI step?
faqs.answer: Yes, when a model is the right worker for a draft or a classification. A person can still approve the result.
